resources.string: A qualitative model of one normal small-intestinal propulsion pattern. Shape, distances, and timing are not to scale. Other intestinal movements and smooth muscle elsewhere can work differently.
A bolus, or small mass of intestinal contents, fills and gently widens the lumen. Inner circular muscle wraps around the tube; outer longitudinal muscle runs along its length.
Circular muscle just downstream of the bolus relaxes. The lumen there can widen to receive the contents.
Circular muscle behind the bolus contracts and narrows the lumen while the region ahead remains relaxed.
Successive sections of the wall squeeze behind the bolus and relax ahead of it. This traveling pattern pushes the contents downstream.
The part of the wall that squeezed relaxes and reopens as the bolus continues downstream.
Human small-intestinal muscle structure (Henrich and Brehler, 1980)
Peristaltic coordination in guinea-pig small intestine (Waterman et al., 1994)
